_comment: Every generator parameter. SYNTHETIC data. Volume is about 0.09 calls per person per year (H-18, Oct 17: 2.25x the 0.04 of H-15/H-16, which was 2x the earlier 0.0198). 0.09 is about 60% of a real US EMS rate of ~0.15, so each xz file is about 22 MB, under the 25 MB limit. H-13 (Oct 16) added day_effect, lateness_seasonality, hour_of_day, congestion and messy_sample, and moved the surge extra calls to their own random stream.
tuning_note: Medians tuned from the starting values (red dispatch 55, turnout 65, eta urban 240 / suburban 330 / rural 780) so the baseline red % late lands in the validate.py bands: urban 5-10, suburban 6-10, rural over 30. Sigmas were not changed. H-16 (Oct 17) doubled only base_rate_per_person_per_year (0.0198 to 0.04) and H-18 (Oct 17) raised it to 0.09; no other parameter was changed, so the planted stories and effect sizes are the same.
drive_slow_outlier_note: Added Oct 16 (decisions brief issue 7): with this probability a call's drive is also multiplied by lognormal(median, sigma), so some ambulances are much slower than the estimate. Drawn last, so all other draws are unchanged.

day_effect.note: H-13. Each (county, day) gets two lognormal(0, sigma) multipliers shared by every ZIP in the county: one on the drive estimate (weather, traffic) and one on the dispatch time (staffing, system load). Seeded from (seed, county_fips), so independent of ZIP order. This makes late counts overdispersed (calls on the same day are not independent). Sigma 0.15 is a tuning choice, not an estimate from real data.

lateness_seasonality.note: H-13. Month multipliers on the MEDIAN drive estimate (winter roads, Dec-Feb x1.10, shoulder months x1.03) and on the median dispatch time (summer x1.05). Not normalized: they multiply the medians directly. Volume month factors above are unchanged.

hour_of_day.note: H-13. Relative arrival rate for local hours 0 to 23 (normalized to mean 1 by the generator): overnight trough about 0.5, afternoon peak about 1.4. A call's time inside its local day is drawn from this profile as a fraction of the day, so 23- and 25-hour daylight-saving days work. dispatch_hour_exponent: dispatch median is also multiplied by weight^exponent (mild: busiest hours +7%, quietest -13%). The profile is invented, not measured.

congestion.note: H-13. Held probability rises with the county-day volume: p_held = held_probability x clip(((count + shrink) / (expected + shrink))^exponent, min, max), where count is that county-day's calls and expected is its calls with no random variation and no surge. shrink_calls keeps tiny counties from reading one extra call as overload. In the surge, the planted extra (summer_surge.held_probability minus held_probability) is added on top.

messy_sample.note: H-13. data/incidents_messy_sample.csv.xz is built from baseline rows of ONE county and ONE month, then problems are injected into disjoint rows. These counts ARE the injection log: validate.py --messy detects each problem type and must find exactly these numbers. The three main files contain none of this.

station_closure.zcta: auto: most populous urban ZCTA in data/lookup/zcta_county.csv

summer_surge.note: H-13. volume_multiplier m: the extra calls are an additional Poisson(expected x (m - 1)) per ZIP and surge day, drawn from a SEPARATE random stream (seed, zcta, 2), so the ordinary calls are drawn exactly as in the baseline and Monroe outside Jul 1 - Aug 31 is identical to baseline. held_probability is the planted level at normal volume; congestion adds a little more.
